words.gram: genitive singular, feminine (with negative не будет)

lines.trans: Straighten your shoulders, you are a real model!
Here is my Elena's favorite dress.
It reminds her of the old days.
Back then she was a poor and unknown singer.
And now she washes the floors at home in it.
She has that kind of home kitchen fitness.
Excellent, the new dress will be ready by evening.
Will you manage to come to our show?
I am afraid I cannot, I have to feed you all.
Then see you tonight at the banquet!
Stop, tell me, who did her makeup?
Hello, what wonderful girls you have!

examples.text: Наш ресторан претендует на высокую награду.
examples.trans: Our restaurant is a contender for a high award.

examples.text: Вы носите еду мимо нашей кассы!
examples.trans: You are carrying food past our cash register!

examples.text: У вас получится прийти на наш показ?
examples.trans: Will you manage to come to our show?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'show / fashion show' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Миша, скоро у нас модный показ.
examples.trans: Misha, soon we will have a fashion show.

examples.text: Показ будет прямо у нас в отеле?
examples.trans: Will the show be right here in our hotel?

examples.text: Отлично, я приеду за день до показа.
examples.trans: Excellent, I will arrive a day before the show.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am afraid'.

examples.text: Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Я не боюсь.
examples.trans: I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам нужно очень хорошо к нему подготовиться.
examples.trans: We need to prepare very well for it.

examples.text: Костя, ты почему так на неё смотрел?
examples.trans: Kostya, why were you staring at her like that?

examples.text: Нет, милая, я никуда не смотрел.
examples.trans: No, darling, I was not looking anywhere.

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will be able to', paired with 'мочь'.

examples.text: Костя, ты почему так на неё смотрел?
examples.trans: Kostya, why were you staring at her like that?

examples.text: Нет, милая, я никуда не смотрел.
examples.trans: No, darling, I was not looking anywhere.

examples.text: Смотри, веди себя тут аккуратно, хорошо?
examples.trans: Mind you behave yourself carefully here, okay?

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Надо придумать, где установить большой подиум.
examples.trans: We need to figure out where to set up the big runway.

examples.text: Мне маму в аэропорту надо встретить.
examples.trans: I need to meet my mom at the airport.

examples.text: Кстати, нам бы теперь рассчитаться надо.
examples.trans: By the way, we should settle up now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'кормить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to feed'.

examples.text: Боюсь, не смогу, надо вас накормить.
examples.trans: I am afraid I cannot, I have to feed you all.

examples.text: Повар вкусно накормил гостей.
examples.trans: The cook fed the guests deliciously.

examples.text: Раз не можем напоить, мы его накормим!
examples.trans: Since we cannot give him drink, we will feed him!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Надо придумать, где установить большой подиум.
examples.trans: We need to figure out where to set up the big runway.

examples.text: Отлично, я приеду за день до показа.
examples.trans: Excellent, I will arrive a day before the show.

examples.text: Будь добр, принеси мне горячий кофе.
examples.trans: Be so kind, bring me a hot coffee.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мне маму в аэропорту надо встретить.
examples.trans: I need to meet my mom at the airport.

examples.text: Тогда до встречи вечером на банкете!
examples.trans: Then see you tonight at the banquet!

examples.text: Я встретил Полину, и всё перевернулось.
examples.trans: I met Polina, and everything turned upside down.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in the evening', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И я тебя люблю, до вечера!
examples.trans: And I love you too, see you tonight!

examples.text: Я вчера вечером захотел в туалет.
examples.trans: Last night I needed to go to the restroom.

examples.text: Отлично, новое платье будет готово к вечеру.
examples.trans: Excellent, the new dress will be ready by evening.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'banquet, feast' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда до встречи вечером на банкете!
examples.trans: Then see you tonight at the banquet!

examples.text: Мы к банкету готовимся, не слышал.
examples.trans: We are preparing for the banquet, I did not hear it.

examples.text: Праздничный банкет.
examples.trans: A festive banquet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'stop, cut', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Будешь красиво на работу в ресторан ходить.
examples.trans: You will walk to work at the restaurant looking beautiful.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, буду рад видеть вас в ресторане.
examples.trans: Hello, I will be glad to see you in the restaurant.

examples.text: Наш ресторан претендует на высокую награду.
examples.trans: Our restaurant is a contender for a high award.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Я ещё ничего не сказала Никите.
examples.trans: I have not said anything to Nikita yet.

examples.text: Зачем ты не сказал, что не бармен?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell her that you are not the bartender?

examples.text: Даже не знаю, как сказать родителям.
examples.trans: I do not even know how to tell my parents.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Извините, а кто вообще этот человек?
examples.trans: Excuse me, and who is this person anyway?

examples.text: Я узнавал, в том номере никто не живёт.
examples.trans: I checked, nobody lives in that room.

examples.text: В номере никто не живёт.
examples.trans: Nobody lives in the room.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'did', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.text: Стоп, скажите, кто делал ей макияж?
examples.trans: Stop, tell me, who did her makeup?

examples.text: Обиделась и совсем не отвечает на звонки.
examples.trans: She got offended and does not answer calls at all.

examples.text: Только смотри не делай как Луи!
examples.trans: Just mind you do not do like Louis!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'makeup' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Стоп, скажите, кто делал ей макияж?
examples.trans: Stop, tell me, who did her makeup?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть макияж.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always makeup.
